messages:
jess_support: FYI escalated from support — customer ACME (acct-234) on Private deployment reporting KMS decrypt failures when we try to read model cache keys. Error started ~2024-06-12 09:10 UTC. They see a 400 from our side saying AccessDeniedException. Pasting the short log they sent below. Can eng-infra + security triage?

liam_infra: Thanks — can you paste the exact KMS key ARN and the decode request id from logs? Also, did they recently rotate keys or change the key policy?

jess_support: Key ARN: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345. Customer says they rotated key last week and added an IAM role for our private runtime. Log snippet: 
```
2024-06-12T09:09:58Z ERROR decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/redwood-private-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345
requestId: c2f4b6d3-9b1a-4f3a-bc12-6e5f4d2a8e55
```

sam_security: Two quick things to check: 1) key policy vs IAM permissions — KMS requires the key policy to allow the principal even if IAM allows it; 2) encryption context mismatch will also give InvalidCiphertextException, but AccessDenied points at policy/role. Did they include an encryption context condition on the key policy (kms:EncryptionContext) or in the PutKeyPolicy?

natalie_custsuccess: I already asked the customer to send their key policy and the IAM role ARN for the runtime. Waiting on that but they said the role is "redwood-private-role" and the role trust allows our service account.

liam_infra: If they rotated key last week, are they re-encrypting data or updating the key id references in our config? If cached model shards were encrypted with the old key, decrypt would fail. Two possible errors: AccessDenied (policy) or InvalidCiphertext (wrong key/context).

jess_support: Customer replied with key policy snippet and says they enforce an encryption context with a service tag. policy snippet: 
```json
{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-private-role"},"Action":"kms:Decrypt","Resource":"*","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"kms:EncryptionContext:service":"acme-service"}}}]}
```

sam_security: aha — they have a condition binding Decrypt to a specific EncryptionContext key. Our runtime must pass the exact encryption context when calling Decrypt. If we previously didn't include it, KMS will deny. Two remediation paths: 1) have our runtime include the encryption context when calling Decrypt; 2) ask customer to relax the key policy (not ideal).

liam_infra: Can you get the client-side call traces? We log the KMS request payloads in private runtime debug mode. If we see missing encryptionContext, that's the culprit. Also confirm whether key rotation created a new key alias or they used same CMK with rotation enabled.

jess_support: Attached the customer's repro steps they provided: 
1) Deploy private runtime config pointing to S3 model-store encrypted with that CMK.
2) Trigger model load via POST /v1/models/load with model_id=acme-v1.
3) Runtime attempts to decrypt chunk metadata -> fails with AccessDenied.
They supplied the KMS request id above.

sam_security: Quick suggested checks for customer (send as checklist):
- Share full key policy and any KMS grants (ListGrants).
- Confirm the encryptionContext key/value used during Encrypt (if any).
- If they rotated keys, confirm whether objects were re-encrypted or encrypted under new key id/alias.
- Check CloudTrail for KMS Decrypt events: eventName=Decrypt, look at userIdentity/arn and errorMessage.

liam_infra: For us: enable debug for the private runtime on their tenant (30m) to capture the outbound KMS call. Command we can run on the node: 
```bash
REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug ./redwood-runtime --tenant acme enable-kms-debug --capture 1800
```
That will capture the request payloads including encryptionContext. Please schedule with customer — might require brief downtime.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-2187 linked to thread 1718202345. Severity: P2. Assignees: liam_infra, sam_security.

jess_support: Customer agreed to a 15m debug window at 09:45 UTC. I'll run the enable-kms-debug command and paste logs.

liam_infra: After we capture logs, primary fixes likely: 
- If missing encryptionContext: update runtime to pass {"service":"acme-service"} when calling KMS Decrypt. Patch should be small — KMS call site already accepts optional context.
- If key policy missing our principal: ask customer to add statement allowing arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-private-role to kms:Decrypt. Example minimal statement: 
```json
{"Sid":"AllowRedwoodDecrypt","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-private-role"},"Action":"kms:Decrypt","Resource":"*"}
```
- For key rotation: ensure model cache is re-encrypted or update config to point at new key.

sam_security: Also remind customer to check for kms:CallerAccount or kms:ViaService conditions in policy; those block cross-account usage unless explicitly allowed.

jess_support: Pasting the debug capture (sanitized): 
```
OUTBOUND KMS Decrypt request id=c2f4b6d3-...
KeyId=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345
CiphertextBlob=...
EncryptionContext={}   <--- empty
```

liam_infra: Confirms root cause: runtime not sending encryptionContext. Quick fix: patch runtime to pull encryption_context from model metadata (we already store optional encryption_context during model upload). I'll open a PR to default to model.metadata.encryption_context when present.

sam_security: Also note follow-up: add an audit alert rule in Console for consecutive KMS Decrypt AccessDenied errors >5 within 5 minutes -> auto escalate.

natalie_custsuccess: Customer is happy with the root cause. They asked about guidance for key rotation to avoid this in future. What do we tell them?

liam_infra: Guidance to send: 
- If you rotate keys, re-encrypt stored objects or use a KMS alias pointing to the new CMK and ensure applications reference the alias.
- Add KMS grants to allow re-encryption operations if using a re-encrypt workflow.
- Keep encryptionContext stable for application-level scoping, and share the expected keys with the runtime.

sam_security: I'll draft a short KB note we can share: how to configure key policy for Redwood Private + sample IAM role and example encryptionContext usage.

jess_support: Thanks everyone — marking as resolved for customer after runtime patch deploy. Will follow up with KB link when ready. :thumbsup:
